reviews.title: Software Update
reviews.text:
I have an older iPhone. I’ve been using a whoop for over three years and it has definitely helped me improve my health and sleep quality. 

I’ve been tracking my whoop data consistently for these three years and making actionable lifestyle changes based on the data. For example, while I knew that eating before bed negatively impacts sleep, but I was able to see the effect clearly from my data. And now I usually can tell when I’m about to get sick a day or two early and can prioritize rest and make cold season less impactful.

But the fact that I have to update my iOS to keep using the app is ridiculous. I don’t want to buy a new phone when this one works perfectly well for everything else. I know that they only mess with the app for job security and to justify price increases because some stressed out zyn-addicted kid from Makenzie promised some disconnected self-important C-Suite employee at Whoop that they would be Deloited at the quarterly reports if they made some unnecessary change. 

I really got value from my Whoop, but I will be canceling my subscription and get off of Whoop when my version of the app is discontinued later this month.

Do better Whoop. Actually, just do less, the product is good enough. Don’t listen to people who don’t care, listen to athletes using the app. You don’t need to change the software, just focus on making the hardware more accurate and ergonomic.

reviews.title: Data incorrect and makes up data
reviews.text:
I’ve used WHOOP for multiple nights, and unfortunately, I’m finding the sleep data to be very inaccurate—especially when I actually have a very poor night of sleep.

On several occasions, WHOOP has reported that I slept great or had a good-quality night, while I personally experienced the opposite. One night in particular was terrible, yet the data didn’t reflect that at all. I’ve now had multiple days where the sleep metrics simply don’t match my actual experience.

For someone who has significant sleep problems, this is a major issue. If the device is consistently telling me that I slept well when I know I didn’t, it makes the sleep scores difficult to trust or use meaningfully.

It may work well for people with relatively normal sleep patterns, but based on my experience, I wouldn’t rely on WHOOP for accurately tracking poor or disrupted sleep.

I figured I would use Whoop for a few months, get a handle on my strain and recovery, and then move on.  But Whoop is just too good and they keep improving and adding additional functionality. I know I am still under-utilizing Whoop and I look forward to incorporating more and more of its features and functionality into my life.

reviews.title: 5.0 does not track caloric expenditure accurately
reviews.text: I’ve used WHOOP 4.0 for 1600 days consecutively and then recently switched to WHOOP 5.0. I used WHOOP specifically to track my caloric expenditure relative to my daily caloric intake using MyFitnessPal. This method worked very well and was very accurate and allowed me to achieve my weight loss goals consistently based on maintaining a daily caloric deficit of 400 cal when I was cutting. Fast forward to August 25 when I switched from 4.0 to WHOOP 5.0 and all of a sudden with no meaningful change in my routine, my caloric expenditure according to WHOOP 5.0 dropped by about 1000 cal per day. Now, even as my weight is flat, WHOOP 5.0 is showing about 1000 cal per day surplus. Very disappointing. I can no longer use WHOOP as an accurate gauge of my daily caloric expenditure.

reviews.title: Login issue after switching to a new iPhone
reviews.text:
I’ve been using WHOOP, but after switching to a new iPhone, I was unable to access my existing account through the iOS app. The app keeps showing a blank “ERROR” message.

My credentials are correct, and I can successfully log into the same account through the WHOOP website and see my membership and payment history. I also reset my password, reinstalled the app, and followed the recommended troubleshooting steps, but the issue remains.

I contacted WHOOP Support and opened a support case, but I still cannot access my account through the app.

It’s extremely frustrating to have an active membership and working account but be unable to use the app after switching phones. I hope WHOOP addresses this issue quickly and improves the login experience.

I would not expect this kind of issue from a paid service.

reviews.text:
I rarely leave negative reviews, but this has been unacceptable.

My WHOOP failed about one week into the free trial in January. I emailed support immediately and repeatedly requested a replacement, but never received a proper resolution. Despite this, I was charged $239, even though I had not approved the payment and my issue had not been resolved.

After months of emails, WHOOP finally confirmed in writing that they would send a complete WHOOP 5.0 replacement and provide the 12 months of Peak membership associated with that charge.

It is now September, more than six months later, and I am still being told they are “investigating.”

I’m not even asking for a refund anymore. I just want WHOOP to honor what they already approved.

reviews.title: I Only Wish WHOOP Had Existed 10 Years Ago
reviews.text:
Since I started using WHOOP, there is one thought I keep coming back to: I wish this had existed 10 years ago.

If I had had this level of insight into my body in my thirties, I am convinced I would have made very different lifestyle choices.

WHOOP has given me something incredibly valuable: awareness.

I have become much more conscious of how much sleep my body actually needs, how much exercise is right for me, how stress affects me, when my body is under pressure even if I don’t necessarily realize it, and what I can do to manage all of this better.

But perhaps one of the biggest surprises has been seeing the impact of my everyday food and lifestyle choices on my recovery.

Things that can seem insignificant like a glass of Prosecco, some fried food, a late or heavy meal, suddenly aren’t so insignificant when you can actually see how your body responds the following day.

WHOOP makes the invisible visible.

And that has changed the way I think about my health. It has made me much more mindful of those small daily decisions that we often underestimate, but that, over time, can have a significant impact on how we feel and perform.

For me, WHOOP isn’t simply a device that tracks data. It has become a tool that helps me understand my body and make better decisions for myself every single day.

I genuinely cannot thank WHOOP enough for existing. I only wish I could go back and give one to my 30-year-old self!

I wish the company and the people behind it every possible success, because I truly believe WHOOP is one of those innovations that can positively change people’s lives.

Absolutely invaluable to me.

reviews.title: Just not helpful
reviews.text:
I got this, hoping that the extra data provided would allow me to gain insight onto how to deal with stress. The stress score is really don’t match with how my body feels either physically or mentally. I can have an extremely difficult day at work and it gives me a low stress score. I can have an easy day at work and have a hard workout it gives me a high stress score.

Those two things are very different and how my body feels them. Additionally, the most stressful day at work can have a score of 4.2 and a 30 minute ride at 60% heart rate gives a 4.2 score. Those are extremely different issues. 

Also, it is difficult to understand because the scores don’t really jibe or relate to how you’re feeling. It produces a lot of data, but I’m not sure if it’s actually reliable or accurate so it’s not worth the extra money or commitment to wearing it at night.
